correctness.rationale: For every n and ordered 1-positions p<q<r, each of the eight length-three subsequence multiplicities is reconstructed exactly from (n,L=2p+q,T=r-p,Q=p^2+q^2+r^2), and conversely three displayed multiplicities recover all three statistics. Fixing L,T makes Q a quadratic in p with at most two integer roots; Vieta gives the unique possible swapped-gap partner. Orient each distinct pair by a>b, set a=b+3h, and count p satisfying p+2b+4h<=n-1. The resulting double sum yields the proposed rational generating function without extrapolating finite data. A separate two-route exhaustive checker verifies all equivalence classes through n=22 and literal deck counts through n=15, reporting VERIFY_OK.

originality.rationale: The directly on-point primary manuscript Chrisnata et al. (2021 early access), section 5.3, explicitly proposes precisely the derived generating function as Conjecture 1, verifies only its first 20 coefficients, and proves only order Theta(n^3). The current result proves it for every n and classifies all fibers by a unique gap swap. Rigo–Salimov (2013) gives the language of binomial equivalence but no such fixed-weight theorem. Actual searches of the mathematical record and the accessible historical corpus returned related but non-dominating results; unindexed later priority remains a risk.
residual_risks: Search indexes do not establish universal novelty; a different or unpublished proof may exist.

value.rationale: Solves the explicit fixed-weight-three 3-deck counting conjecture in Chrisnata et al., which was supported by only finite coefficients and an asymptotic order bound. The result gives full equivalence-class structure, an all-length exact rational series and direct optimal fixed-content readout code size. A sharp natural sequence-reconstruction problem, not a routine increment or arbitrary parameter slice.
